title: Power Pages: first-class support for Power Platform connector APIs
summary: Hold: the endpoint-filtering route omits the admin centre navigation and the step to edit the policy, so readers cannot follow it as printed. The roadmap facts match the record; the licensing field also understates the published product-level licensing.

claims.claim: The roadmap item concerns first-class connector API support in Power Pages.
claims.quote: Power Pages: First Class Support for Connector APIs in Power Pages

claims.claim: The feature is in development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: General availability is listed for June CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2027"

claims.quote: "previewDate": "March CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 2026-10-26T23:15:50.
Microsoft plans native Power Platform connector support for Power Pages websites.
claims.quote: Native connectors support through Power Pages will allow organizations to securely connect their websites/portals directly to enterprise systems

claims.claim: The roadmap names SQL, SAP and Oracle as enterprise-system examples.
claims.quote: enterprise systems such as SQL, SAP, and Oracle

claims.claim: The planned native support removes the need to build or maintain a custom integration layer.
claims.quote: without building or maintaining custom integration layers.

claims.claim: The roadmap highlights regulated customers with data behind corporate firewalls.
claims.quote: especially valuable for regulated and enterprise customers such as banking and financial services, who need to surface data from systems hosted behind corporate firewalls.

claims.claim: The planned capability leverages the Power Platform on-premises data gateway.
claims.quote: By leveraging the Power Platform on-premises data gateway and connector framework

claims.claim: The planned capability uses the connector framework.
claims.quote: By leveraging the Power Platform on-premises data gateway and connector framework

claims.claim: The roadmap describes server-side logic that can interact with on-premises data sources.
claims.quote: gaining the flexibility to build server-side logic that can interact with on-premises data sources.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The roadmap promises consistent security and governance with existing Power Platform policies.
claims.quote: Customers benefit from consistent security, governance, and compliance with existing Power Platform policies

claims.claim: Learn does not yet document the planned native connector API capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connector APIs documentation connector framework on-premises; Power Pages native connectors server logic connection identity per visitor authorization supported operations SQL SAP Oracle. Read Server logic overview and Power Pages capabilities excerpts.

claims.claim: The default state of native connector API support is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native Power Platform connector APIs on-premises gateway default enable site settings admin API pac pages Dataverse. Read roadmap description, Server logic overview and Configure site settings excerpts; no native-connector default stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Licensing specific to native connector APIs is unpublished, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to mixed. Replace licensing.notes with 'Power Pages uses Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month capacity subscriptions or pay-as-you-go meters. Additional licensing specific to native connector APIs is not yet published.' Replace the opening 'Not yet published.' in Cost and licensing with 'Additional licensing specific to native connector APIs is not yet published.' Keep the existing licensing FAQ citation.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy reaches connector governance.
claims.quote: select Security ... select Data and privacy ... select Data policy ... select New Policy to create a new policy to configure.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and the rendered route to 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Block'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/prevent-data-loss for connector classification; its walkthrough documents the Pre-built connectors page and the Block action for blockable connectors. State in the row note that only blockable connectors can be blocked.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy creates the data policy that determines connector use.
claims.quote: Creates a new DLP policy in the tenant by using the NewPolicy DLPPolicyDefinition object. ... New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy ... Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/data-loss-prevention-sdk to sources: it documents creating policies that classify connectors into Business, Non-business and Blocked groups. Add to the row note: 'Creates a policy from the supplied policy definition; connector classifications must be included in that definition.'

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Data policy > policy > Prebuilt Connectors > connector > Configure connector > Connector endpoints is the endpoint-filtering route.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Security ... select Data and privacy ... select Data policy. ... Select an existing policy on the command bar and then select Edit policy
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path and the rendered route with 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit policy > Prebuilt Connectors > connector > Configure connector > Connector endpoints'. The navigation and Edit policy step are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/connector-action-control; the final steps are documented at the existing endpoint-filtering URL.

claims.claim: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations with TenantId, PolicyName and NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations creates endpoint-filtering rules for a policy.
claims.quote: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId $TenantId -PolicyName $PolicyName -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations $ConnectorConfigurations

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn has not confirmed how classic data policies apply to native Power Pages connector APIs.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connector APIs data policies DLP connector endpoint filtering governance. Read Data policies, Manage data policies, Connector action control and Power Pages governance excerpts; documented workload reach does not explicitly settle native Power Pages APIs.

claims.claim: Learn has not confirmed endpoint filtering applies to native Power Pages connector APIs.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connector APIs data policies DLP connector endpoint filtering governance. Read Connector endpoint filtering: its reach is apps, flows and chatbots and their designers, without documenting native Power Pages connector APIs.

claims.claim: A Power Pages-specific native connector API control is not documented on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connector APIs enable disable control Power Platform API pac pages PowerApps Administration PowerShell Dataverse connector site setting entity reference. Read Use Power Pages admin APIs, site-setting, CLI, PowerShell and connector-table excerpts; no feature-specific control.

claims.claim: Connector endpoint filtering is preview.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: Endpoint filtering is available when Endpoint configurable is Yes.
claims.quote: If the value of the Endpoint configurable column is Yes, you can use this capability by right-clicking and then selecting Configure connector > Connector endpoints.

claims.claim: Endpoint filtering evaluates static designer endpoints, not dynamically bound runtime endpoints.
claims.quote: Endpoint filtering rules aren't enforced on environment variables, custom inputs, and dynamically bound endpoints during runtime. Only static endpoints that are known and selected when building an app, flow, or chatbot during design time are enforced.

claims.claim: Per-visitor authorisation for native connector API data is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connectors server logic connection identity per visitor authorization supported operations SQL SAP Oracle. Read Server logic overview and Power Pages security; general session, web-role and Dataverse table permissions do not state native connector data authorisation.

claims.claim: Connection identity for the planned native connector capability is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connectors server logic connection identity per visitor authorization supported operations SQL SAP Oracle. Read Server logic overview and Data policies; neither specifies the identity used by native Power Pages connectors.

claims.claim: Per-visitor delegation for the planned native connector capability is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connectors server logic connection identity per visitor authorization supported operations SQL SAP Oracle. Read Server logic overview and Power Pages security; no native-connector per-visitor delegation mechanism stated.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports POST to send data to external systems.
claims.quote: POST ... Create records or send new data. ... Commonly used to insert new records into Dataverse or send data to external systems.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports PUT for updates or replacements.
claims.quote: Server logic supports standard HTTP methods to perform operations on data or interact with external services. ... PUT ... Updates or replaces an entire record or dataset.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports PATCH for partial updates.
claims.quote: PATCH ... Updates part of a record (upsert). ... Performs a partial update of existing data without replacing the entire record.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports DELETE to remove data from an external system.
claims.quote: DELETE ... Removes records or data from Dataverse or an external system.

claims.claim: Supported operations for the planned native connector capability are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connectors server logic connection identity per visitor authorization supported operations SQL SAP Oracle. Read Server logic overview and connector-reference excerpts; these document general server logic and other connector workloads, not native Power Pages operations.

claims.claim: Gateway hosting charges specific to native Power Pages connector APIs are unpublished.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connector APIs licensing premium connectors gateway charges capacity anonymous users. Read Power Platform licensing FAQs and gateway-management excerpts; no gateway hosting charge specific to native Power Pages connector APIs stated.

claims.claim: Additional capacity charges specific to native Power Pages connector APIs are unpublished.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connector APIs licensing premium connectors gateway charges capacity anonymous users. Read Power Platform licensing FAQs and capacity-management excerpts; website capacity is documented, but no additional native-connector capacity charge is stated.

claims.claim: Power Pages sites are available to internal users by default.
claims.quote: By default, all Power Pages sites are available to users who are internal to your organization.

claims.claim: The public visibility setting makes a Power Pages site accessible anonymously over the Internet.
claims.quote: The public setting makes the site accessible to everyone over the Internet anonymously or to users authenticated through identity providers.
